name: write/email
title: Draft an email
summary: Draft an email or message: purpose first, the facts the user gave and nothing invented, a clear ask, a fitting tone.
when: Use when the user asks for an email or message to be written to someone.
steps: Name the reader, the purpose and the tone in one line before writing a word of the draft.
Call recall with query set to the reader's name and limit 6 to find facts the user saved earlier.
Include only facts the user gave or recall returned; leave any missing detail as a blank the user fills.
Order the draft: greeting, the purpose in the first sentence, the facts, one clear ask, closing.
Call note with action save, title set to the subject and content set to the draft, so the user keeps a copy.
Call clipboard with action write and text set to the draft, so the user can paste it into their mail program.
Say plainly that Kiwibro cannot send email, so this is a draft to copy and send by hand.
Answer with the draft itself and one line naming the blanks left for the user to fill.
next: The final answer must be the finished draft with the facts that were given, one clear ask, the blanks left marked, and a line saying it was not sent.
